## s01_title | title | O1
template: title
narrator: Welcome. In the next few minutes, you'll learn how to get your expense claims paid quickly, and correctly.
claim: This lesson covers submitting expense claims at Northwind Co. [general]

## s02_hook | hook | O1
template: stat
visual: Pile of crumpled receipts next to a laptop.
narrator: Last year, ^ almost one in five expense claims came back to the employee. The reason? A missing receipt.
claim: In 2025, 18% of expense claims were returned because a receipt was missing. [S01#c1]

## s03_rules | rules | O1
template: bullets
narrator: Three rules keep your claim moving. ^ Keep a receipt for anything over twenty-five dollars. ^ Submit within thirty days. ^ And remember, after ninety days, a claim isn't paid at all.
claim: A receipt is required for every expense over $25. [S01#c1]
claim: Expense claims must be submitted within 30 days of the expense date. [S01#c1]
claim: Claims older than 90 days are not reimbursed. [S01#c1]

## s04_steps | steps | O2
template: steps
narrator: Here's the claim, step by step. ^ Photograph the receipt the same day. ^ Open the Northwind Expenses app and start a new claim. ^ Add the category, date, amount and purpose. ^ Attach the receipt and submit it to your approver.
claim: Keep the itemised receipt and photograph it on the same day. [S01#c1]
claim: Open the Northwind Expenses app and select New Claim. [S01#c1]
claim: Attach the receipt photo to each line and submit the claim to your approver. [S01#c1]

## s05_mistake | mistakes | O3
template: do_dont
rookie: The hotel was two hundred and sixty dollars. I'll just split it into two claims. {instr: "casual, a bit too pleased"}
narrator: ^ Don't. Splitting a bill to stay under an approval limit is never allowed. ^ Instead, submit it once, and ask the Travel Desk about the hotel cap.
claim: Never split one expense into several claims to stay under an approval limit. [S01#c1]
claim: Hotel costs are capped at $220 per night unless the Travel Desk approves an exception. [S01#c1]

template: quiz
narrator: Quick check. You bought a twelve-dollar taxi ride. Do you need a receipt? {pause: 2.2}
narrator: ^ No. Receipts are required for expenses over twenty-five dollars, but keeping one never hurts.

claim: Scenario: a $12 taxi ride (fictional example). [general]
